title: Indoor Turf in the Denver Metro | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Indoor turf for Denver-area gyms and studios, planned around the code at your address: floor-finish tests, permits and who to ask. Free visit and written price.
h1: Indoor turf for your gym, planned around the code at your address.
lede: Get sled lanes, sprint tracks and training floors planned around your building’s code from the first drawing. Across the Denver metro, the code edition and the office that enforces it change from one address to the next, so we plan the turf, pad and layout around the answers for yours.
wins: The code edition and fire office for your address, found first
Turf and pad with test reports that match where they go
Lanes and markings laid out around exits and corridors

answer.question: Does indoor turf in a Denver-area gym have to meet a fire code?
answer.answer: Expect it to. Denver’s floor-finish section exempts wood, vinyl and similar traditional floors, and resilient coverings not made of fibers. It does not name turf, so the building department decides how yours is treated. If the rules apply, the turf must pass the pill test or ASTM D2859, and corridors need more unless the building is sprinklered throughout. Outside Denver, the edition depends on who enforces the code at the address. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

blocks.h2: The code edition can change at the city line.
paras: Denver works from the 2024 International Building Code and Fire Code with its own amendments, published as the 2025 Denver Building Code and the 2025 Denver Fire Code. The city amended both again in November 2025, so work from a copy that includes those changes. As of 12 September 2026, Aurora’s building division lists the 2021 editions of both codes.

In some suburbs a fire protection district reviews the plans, and one district can work from several editions. West Metro Fire Rescue handles plan review, permits and inspections for new construction and changes to existing buildings. Its code table, checked on 12 September 2026, lists the 2021 International Fire Code for Lakewood, the 2024 edition for unincorporated Jefferson County and the 2018 edition for unincorporated Douglas County. It also warns that some unincorporated Jefferson County properties have a city or town mailing address, and points to the county assessor’s records to tell them apart.
For any other address, the building department can tell you which edition it enforces and which fire department or district reviews the plans. Those two answers set the tests your turf and pad need.

blocks.h2: In Denver, a new use needs a new certificate.
paras: Denver’s exempt-work list, Section 130.3 of the building code, includes floor coverings and carpeting, and says such items shall comply with Chapter 8, the interior finishes chapter. The same section says an exemption does not authorize work that breaks the code.

A change of use is a separate question. Under Section 142.2, no building or part of one may be used for an occupancy other than the one on its Certificate of Occupancy until the building official issues a new one. Section 133.1 counts a change of use or occupancy as work that affects life safety, which keeps it off the list of interior alterations that can be drawn without an architect or engineer. Turning a warehouse or shop unit into a training floor? Ask Denver’s building department about the new certificate before you sign the lease.

The building official decides the classification. Denver’s Chapter 3 lists gymnasiums without spectator seating in Group A-3, and training and skill development outside a school, such as martial arts and gymnastics, in Group B where it is not classified as assembly.

blocks.h2: Get fire-test reports for the turf and pad together.
paras: Denver’s amendments leave Section 804, the floor-finish section, as the International Code Council published it (third-party copy). Its exception covers traditional floors such as wood, vinyl, linoleum and terrazzo, and resilient coverings not made of fibers. It does not mention turf, so ask the building department whether yours will be reviewed as a floor covering.

If it is, it must pass the DOC FF-1 pill test or ASTM D2859 in every occupancy. Carpet-type coverings are tested as proposed for use, including underlayment, and the reports go to the building official on request. Stairway and ramp enclosures, exit passageways, corridors and rooms not walled off from a corridor to the ceiling need at least a Class II radiant-flux rating in Groups A and B. In a building sprinklered throughout under Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2, pill-test materials are allowed there instead.
Tell us whether the turf reaches any of those areas and whether the building is fully sprinklered, so the product you choose comes with the right report.

blocks.h2: Gluing the turf down? Settle the fire-code permit first.
paras: The 2025 Denver Fire Code, in its December 2025 version, requires an operational permit for floor finishing or surfacing operations over 350 square feet using Class I or Class II liquids. It does not say whether gluing turf counts. The code makes the Denver Fire Department Prevention Division the agency that enforces it, and the official in charge of the Division is the fire code official.
If the layout calls for adhesive, get the product’s liquid class from its supplier, then put the permit question to the Division before the install date is set.

blocks.h2: Bring your code answers to the free visit.
paras: On the free visit we measure the training space, check the existing floor and talk through lanes, markings and transitions. You get a custom layout and a written price to approve before work starts.

Bring the address, a floor plan showing corridors and exits, whether the building is sprinklered, and any landlord or school approval steps. The indoor turf service covers turf, pad and marking choices. For outdoor turf, see the Denver metro page and our Colorado turf guide.

faq.q: My gym is in Aurora. What changes?
faq.a: Your questions go to Aurora, not Denver. Aurora works from older code editions, and Denver’s amendments, including its permit exemption for floor coverings and its floor-finishing permit, apply in Denver only. Ask Aurora’s building division whether a turf floor needs a permit and which fire-test reports it wants to see.

faq.q: Can a public or charter school put turf in its gym?
faq.a: Start with the Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control. Its school construction page says work on public schools, institute charter schools, charter schools and junior colleges that is not maintenance or service needs a permit and must follow the Division’s adopted codes. On 12 September 2026, the Division’s adopted-codes page listed the 2021 building and fire codes, while West Metro Fire Rescue’s table listed the 2024 fire code for the state public schools program. Ask the Division which edition your project falls under.

faq.q: Does Colorado’s PFAS law reach an indoor turf floor?
faq.a: Its wording is broad. SB24-081, as signed, says that on and after January 1, 2026, a person shall not install artificial turf containing intentionally added PFAS chemicals on any portion of property in the state. It still lets you maintain turf installed before that date. Get written PFAS documentation from the manufacturer, and see does artificial turf contain PFAS? for what it should cover.
